'''''Jatropha multifida''''', called '''coral plant''', '''coralbush''', and '''physic nut''' (a name it shares with other members of its genus), is a species of ''[[Jatropha]]'' native to Mexico and the Caribbean.<ref name="314308-2" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:314308-2 |title=''Jatropha multifida'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=11 September 2020 }}</ref> A garden plant, it has been introduced to Florida, and to many places in South America, Africa, the Indian subcontinent, China and Southeast Asia. Mildly toxic, consumption causes gastrointestinal distress.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/s0736-4679(00)00207-9 |title=Rare ''Jatropha multifida'' intoxication in two children |year=2000 |last1=Levin |first1=Yotam |last2=Sherer |first2=Yaniv |last3=Bibi |first3=Haim |last4=Schlesinger |first4=Menachem |last5=Hay |first5=Emile |journal=The Journal of Emergency Medicine |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=173–175 |pmid=10903468 }}</ref>
